title: Fall of a bound pair of two bodies in a sharp field

key_results.statement: For the sharp stationary field start, $C(\Psi\otimes\varphi)=((C_{\rm red}+e_f)\Psi)\otimes\varphi$ with $C_{\rm red}=\sum_i[A_i+\sum_xP^{(i)}_x\otimes(1+g_ix)G_i+\kappa\hat x_i\otimes X]+U$, the contract of an admissible description of $b_1,b_2,c$; a binding with a factor of the field would need a three-object term, which (1.10) does not contain.

$C_{\rm bod}=C^{\rm D}_1+C^{\rm D}_2+U+\sum_ig_i\hat x_i\otimes G_i+\kappa\langle X\rangle(\hat x_1+\hat x_2)$, fixed by $C$, $\chi$, $\varphi$ up to an additive constant; $g_1$, $g_2$, $\kappa\langle X\rangle$ are fixed by $C_{\rm bod}$ and well defined.

On the levels the gradient terms are $\hat X_\eta\mathcal K+\hat r\mathcal D_\eta$ with $\mathcal K=g_1M_1\sigma^{(1)}_3+g_2M_2\sigma^{(2)}_3+2\kappa\langle X\rangle$ independent of $\eta$ and $\mathcal D_\eta=\mathcal D_0-\eta\mathcal K$, which depends on $\eta$ unless all gradients vanish.

For every binding of $\mathcal W$, every bound level and every packet of $\mathcal G(\mathcal P_0)$, the first-order velocities of both parts are $v^{(1)}_i(\lambda)=\lambda\langle\alpha\rangle_g+\rho_i(\lambda)$ with the same coefficient, $\alpha(P)=-E_b''\langle\mathcal K\rangle_P+E_b'\partial_P\langle\mathcal K\rangle_P$.

The rest $\rho_i$ of the first-order velocity is an explicit oscillating term with $\rho_i(0)=0$ and $\lvert\rho_i(\lambda)\rvert\le\tau_i\mathsf B_g$ for all $\lambda$, where $\mathsf B_g$ is finite because the level is isolated on the support of $g$ and $g'$ is square integrable.

The first-order change of the mean label separation is $\lambda\langle\beta\rangle_g+\sigma(\lambda)$ with bounded $\sigma$ and $\beta=-\langle\mathcal K\rangle_P\partial_P\langle\hat r\rangle_P-2E_b'\,\mathrm{Re}\langle\hat r\psi_P\vert R_P\vert\mathcal K\psi_P\rangle$; there is no term in $\lambda^2$, and $\beta\equiv0$ if $W(-r)^{*}=W(r)$, in particular for every diagonal on-site binding.

With the window average first and the sharp-total-label limit second, the drift acceleration of both parts at $P_0$ is $g_1\alpha_1(P_0)+g_2\alpha_2(P_0)+\kappa\langle X\rangle\alpha_X(P_0)$ with $\alpha_i=-M_i[E_b''\partial_{M_i}E_b-E_b'\partial_{M_i}E_b']$, $\alpha_X=-2E_b''$; in the other order the limit does not exist on the class in general.

For the common gradient the coefficient is $-E_b''\mathcal M_P+E_b'\mathcal M_P'$ with $\mathcal M_P=M_1\langle\sigma^{(1)}_3\rangle_P+M_2\langle\sigma^{(2)}_3\rangle_P=E_b-\langle A_1\rangle_P-\langle A_2\rangle_P-\langle U\rangle_P$: only the rest terms of the scaling relation enter.

For a diagonal on-site binding at leading order in $\mathsf R$ and fixed $u$, the drift acceleration of the pair from rest is $a_{\rm pair}=\frac{\varsigma}{\sqrt{1+u^2}}\frac{g_1M_1+g_2M_2+2\kappa\langle X\rangle}{\mathfrak m_1+\mathfrak m_2}$ with relative remainders $O(\epsilon^2)$, i.e. $-\varsigma(1+u^2)^{-1/2}$ times the inertia-weighted mean $\bar a$ of the free falls.
Ordered limits: $a_{\rm pair}\to-\varsigma\bar a[1-u^2/2+O(u^4)]$ for $u\to0$ and $a_{\rm pair}\to-\varsigma\bar a/u\to0$ for $u\to\infty$.

For $\langle X\rangle=0$, $a_{\rm pair}/a^{(i)}=-\frac{\varsigma}{\sqrt{1+u^2}}\frac{g_1M_1+g_2M_2}{g_i\tau_i^2(\mathfrak m_1+\mathfrak m_2)}$: even when the free parts fall alike the ratio is $-\varsigma/\sqrt{1+u^2}\neq1$ at every fixed $u$, so the pair falls like its parts only for $w_{11}<0$ in the ordered wide-pair limit.

At leading order in $\mathsf R$, $a_{\rm pair}=\varsigma(g_1M_1+g_2M_2+2\kappa\langle X\rangle)/\sqrt{(\mathfrak m_1+\mathfrak m_2)^2+16w^2\mathfrak m_1^2\mathfrak m_2^2}$ is the same for all pairs of clock levels iff $g_1=g_2=0$ and $\kappa\langle X\rangle=0$.

At zeroth order in the gradients the rate of the clock of the part $i$ of a pair at rest at the label $x_0$ is $r_i(x_0)=\frac{1+g_ix_0}{\lambda_{0,i}}\Gamma_i(x_0)$ with $\Gamma_i=1-\frac{\tau_i^2}{4n_i^2\bar M_i^2}\Lambda(x_0)+O(\epsilon^4)$, $n_i=1+g_ix_0$.

The relative change of the clock rate per label is $\varrho_i=g_i+\frac{\tau_i^2}{4\bar M_i^2}[2\Lambda g_i+\frac{\varsigma u^2}{(1+u^2)^{3/2}}\frac{g_1a_1+g_2a_2}{a}]$, equal to $g_i$ at leading order.

$\mathsf w_i^2=-a_{\rm pair}/\varrho_i=-\frac{\varsigma}{\sqrt{1+u^2}}\frac{g_1M_1+g_2M_2}{g_i(\mathfrak m_1+\mathfrak m_2)}$ at leading order: it is not $\tau_i^2$, it is the same for both parts at leading order iff $g_1=g_2$, and it contains the binding and the clock levels.

For the common gradient and $\tau_1=\tau_2=\tau$ the pair obeys the relation of the form (4.24) with $v_{\max}^2$ replaced by $-\varsigma v_{\max}^2/\sqrt{1+u^2}$; with the speed $\tau d_0$ it holds only for $w_{11}<0$ in the ordered wide-pair limit, with the leading deviation $-u^2/2$.

open_issues: The second order in the gradients and the range of λ over which the first order describes the motion are not estimated; (13.9) and (13.10) bound first-order terms only.
The limit δP → 0 at a fixed window is only shown not to exist on the class in general; the quantity it defines on a subclass is not characterized.
A binding of the class W with β not identically zero is exhibited numerically (set S5), not analytically.

The relative remainders O(ε²) of (13.13)–(13.20) are not determined (numerically up to 4 % at τ/M = 0.2) and are not uniform in u; the ε² term of (13.18) assumes a differentiable remainder of (11.20).
The first-order corrections to the clock reading of a pair in the field (the gradient across the packet) are not derived.
The results hold for a binding and for motion terms without a factor of the field; whether another admissible coupling makes the pair fall like its parts is outside this package.

consistency_checks.check: One body and no binding: (13.8) applied to one free body reproduces (4.7) with g_ζ = 0 for all p and both branches; the ordered limit u → 0 with w11 < 0 of (13.13) is the inertia-weighted mean of the free falls.
Common gradient against the scaling relation (11.6): with (11.14) at P = 0 both sides of (13.12) equal M1 + M2 − aΛ.
